ideas.title: Trade-history secondary index diet: one packed row per (trader, block) instead of two 106-byte rows per fill
ideas.area: torus-bridge native_executor.rs TradeKvs / bg_writer / torus-rpc get_user_trades
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Replace the maker+taker CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES rows (key 32 B, value 74 B each, a full copy of the primary payload: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:238-300) with one row per (trader, block): key = trader(20)+desc_block(8), value = list of (market_id 8, trade_index 4, role 1) = 13 B per fill. Build it in pass B with a HashMap<Address, Vec<u8>> keyed by trader (or in the writer, see idea 2). Keep CF_NATIVE_TRADES (primary) unchanged. 2) Change crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1674-1730 get_user_trades to scan the packed rows newest-first and point-get CF_NATIVE_TRADES by (market, block, idx) for price/qty/side/timestamp (limit <= 1000 gets). 3) Version byte on the new row format; fresh genesis for the devnet (node-local CFs, not in NATIVE_ROOT_CFS, so no consensus change). 4) Validate first with a zero-risk ceiling probe: an env flag that skips the secondary rows entirely (3+3 interleaved cells), watching torus_rocksdb_wal_bytes, torus_rocksdb_compaction_cpu_micros, the torus-trade-writer and rocksdb:low thread CPU in threads.log, trade_writer_queued_batches, and matched/s.
ideas.reasoning: Per native block val0 settles 21,329,405/367 = 58,118 fills and emits 3 rows per fill = 174k rows and 58,118 x 297 B = 17.3 MB, of which the secondary index is 116k rows and 12.3 MB. RocksDB wrote 12.607 GB of WAL in the 300 s cell = 34.4 MB per native block, so the secondary index alone is 36% of the node's WAL volume and trade history in total is 50%. The packed form is 116k x 13 B + <= 2.8k keys (distinct traders per block are bounded by the 1,026,261/367 = 2,796 dirty (trader,market) position rows) = ~1.6 MB and <= 2.8k rows: -10.7 MB WAL per block (-31% per node) and -113k memtable inserts per block. CPU is the cost, not I/O: the disk is 17.7% utilized with 2.1 ms fsyncs, while the torus-trade-writer thread averages 0.40 core per node (14% of its samples runnable-but-waiting) and the RocksDB background threads 0.92 core per node (3 x rocksdb:low at 23.9% + rocksdb:high at 19.7%); cf_native_user_trades has 8 L0 files, the most of any CF (trades 2, positions 1), because trader-prefixed keys are random-insert and every L0->L1 rewrites the CF, while the primary (market, block, idx) keys are append-ordered. Attributing 67% of writer rows and 40-60% of background CPU to the secondary index frees 0.6-0.8 core per node = 1.8-2.4 cores host-wide (10-13% of 18 cores; take 1.2-2.4). The s64 item-6 arithmetic maps a 0.4-host-CPU relief to ~+17% blk/s; scaling linearly, 0.07-0.13 gives +3-5.5%; after dilution take +2-5% matched/s. The hotstuff-algo thread shows 9.4% runqueue wait in the same sampler, so CPU relief does reach consensus.

ideas.title: Hand owned Vec<Fill> to the trade writer and build trade rows off the exec thread
ideas.area: torus-bridge native_executor.rs settle pass A/B, torus-consensus app.rs trade handoff, torus-state bg_writer
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Stop building TradeKvs in pass A (compute_market_settle_plan, native_executor.rs:4507-4515) and stop the move+stamp+push loop in pass B (:4400-4408 and the sequential :4088-4090). 2) After pass B, for each market in id order and each successful order in order, std::mem::take(&mut result.fills) into a Vec<(MarketId, Vec<Fill>)> (fills are already owned by PlaceResult and have no consumer after settlement: no `.fills` use in app.rs or torus-rpc). 3) Submit (height, timestamp, fills) to BackgroundCfWriter at the same handoff point as today (app.rs:2001/2138); the writer assigns trade_index as a running counter in that canonical order (identical key sequence to today) and encodes rows there, in the compact format of idea 1 if that lands. 4) Remove OrderSettlePlan.trades and PackedCfBatch regrowth on E. Validate: byte-identical CF_NATIVE_TRADES/USER_TRADES contents vs the current path on a fixture block (the trade_kvs_tests oracle), then A/B on exec_settle_pass_b_seconds and exec_settle_pass_a_seconds.
ideas.reasoning: Settle pass B is 42.35 s / 367 = 115.4 ms per native block, serial on the exec thread, and pass A is 90.8 ms wall; settle in total is 216 ms of the ~700 ms per native block on E. Per fill the E side currently moves a 297 B TradeKvs out of a per-order Vec, stamps six fields, and does three arena pushes (~600 B memcpy) into a PackedCfBatch that is mem::take'n every block and regrows from empty to 17.3 MB (doubling copies of ~17 MB plus ~4.2k page faults). At streaming rates that is 250-500 ns per fill x 58,118 fills = 15-30 ms, plus 40-58k per-order Vec<TradeKvs> alloc/free pairs (3-5 ms) and the fresh-arena page faults (2-4 ms): 20-40 ms off E's ~700 ms per native block = -3 to -6% exec time. Exec is the limiter only in the last ~120 s of a 300 s cell (exec busy 0.91-0.93), so the 300 s effect is roughly 0.4 x 3-6% = +1-2.5% matched/s now; it rises to +3-6% once the planned consensus items (A-C, s64 #1) make exec the limiter across the whole window. The fills themselves are 58k x 112 B = 6.5 MB already allocated by the matching engine, so no new E-side allocation.

ideas.title: Trade-writer backlog is a memory and backpressure cliff: bound by bytes, recycle the arena, adaptive priority
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs trade_writer, torus-state bg_writer.rs, tools/matched-bench summarize.py
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Track queued bytes in BackgroundCfWriter (sum of PackedCfBatch.bytes.len() + rows.len()*32) and export torus_trade_writer_queued_bytes; add it and queued_batches to summarize.py per-minute output. 2) Make low_pri adaptive: chunks are written low_pri only while queued_batches <= 4; above that use normal priority (the existing TORUS_BG_WRITER_LOW_PRI plumbing at bg_writer.rs:162-182 and write_rows_chunked). 3) Recycle the arena: the writer returns the drained Vec<u8>/rows Vecs through a small channel and take_pending_trade_batch reuses their capacity, so E stops regrowing a 17 MB arena and page-faulting it every block. 4) Replace the batch-count cap 256 (app.rs:3262) with a byte cap (e.g. 512 MB) and, on overflow, write that batch synchronously on the writer at normal priority instead of blocking E in send_packed.
ideas.reasoning: sampler.csv for val0 shows trade_writer_queued_batches at 0, 3, 2, 2, 5, 9, 13, 16 over the first 210 s, then 40, 42, 57, 66 over the last 120 s (the exec-bound window): arrivals are 367/300 = 1.22 batches/s while the writer drains ~1.0/s, and in the late window the gap is ~0.42 batches/s. Each queued batch holds a 17.3 MB arena plus 174k x 32 B row descriptors = ~23 MB, so 66 batches pin ~1.5 GB of RSS per node at cell end; the s64 report attributes RSS growth of 124 MB -> 7.7 GB to the allocator, and this queue is ~20% of it. The channel is a sync_channel(256) whose send blocks when full (bg_writer.rs send_batch -> tx.send), so at the late-window growth rate the cap is reached after roughly 256/0.42 = 10 min of sustained load, after which the exec thread blocks in send_packed for about one writer batch (~1 s) per block: an exec stall the 300 s cells never reach but a longer run or production would. The writer drains slowly because chunks are low_pri (RocksDB deprioritizes them under compaction debt: cf_native_user_trades sits at 8 L0 files) and the thread itself waits on the runqueue 14% of the time.

Evidence that changes existing estimates or premises (all from /home/18c/bench-results-matched/s65-votefix-ctl-r1 val0 and its host sampler, code at /home/18c/projects/wt/s63-body-fetch @ f05b20e):
1. Per-fill settlement state writes are already well batched: 1,026,261 dirty position rows / 367 native blocks = 2,796 rows per block against 58,118 fills (~20 RMWs absorbed per row by PositionCache), 492 dirty balances per block, cache_flush 5.5 ms per block. A cross-block resident position/balance cache (the obvious lever for this angle) would save only the ~2.8k cold reads per block (~3 ms, reads hit the parent FrozenPending BTreeMap or the memtable). Not worth doing. The overlay's journal `record` (backend.rs:369-372) is free when no checkpoint is open, so there is no hidden per-put cost either.
2. The real per-fill write is trade history: 3 rows / 297 B per fill = 174k rows and 17.3 MB per native block per node, 50% of the 12.6 GB of WAL each node wrote in 300 s (42 MB/s per node, 131 MB/s host disk). Storage is still not the blocker (sda 17.7% util, f_await 2.1 ms, write_stall 0), but the CPU is: trade writer 0.40 core/node, RocksDB background threads 0.92 core/node (compaction_cpu_micros 259 s in a 300 s cell), i.e. ~4 of the host's 18 cores go to writing and compacting node-local history. This sharpens the s64 'disable_wal for trade history' item: WAL-off removes the 6.3 GB of WAL bytes but none of the memtable-insert or compaction CPU, which the row diet (idea 1) does.
3. Bench realism gap: the generator fixes one side per (sender, market) (tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:577-611, test at :709), so positions never close; the realized-PnL credit path (apply_fill_via_caches -> bal_cache) and the position tombstone path are never exercised under load, and position sizes grow monotonically (~7k fills per pair per cell). No perf risk found (a close costs one cached balance RMW), but the settle-path numbers do not cover closes/flips.
4. torus_state_root_compute_seconds has count 0: the native root now runs inside the flush worker (flush_worker_seconds 101 ms avg per job, state_write_db 175 ms per native block) and exec_handoff_wait is 1.4 s per cell, so root and state_write are off the critical path; W is not a lever right now.
5. Sampler artefact: pidstat names the exec thread and its scoped match/settle workers alike ('torus-execution', 23,119 samples ~ 59 threads across 3 nodes), so per-thread CPU for the exec chain cannot be read from threads.log without TIDs; the hotstuff-algo, trade-writer and rocksdb threads are unambiguous.
6. cf_native_user_trades has 8 L0 files at cell end versus 2 for cf_native_trades and 1 for positions: the trader-prefixed secondary index is the CF RocksDB is falling behind on, consistent with the low_pri writer backlog growing fastest in the exec-bound late window (16 -> 66 queued batches over the last 120 s).

ideas.reasoning: Nothing consumes the maintained root: `agreement.jsonl` shows `header_state_root` = 0x0 on all three nodes and `torus_state_root_compute_seconds_count` is 0 for the whole window, so CF_NATIVE_TRIE/CF_NATIVE_HASHED are write-only. Cost per native block on val0 (s64-confirm-main-r1, 391 native blocks/300 s): root wall 110 ms of the 389 ms W flush; dirty entries 3284 (positions 2683, balances 472, books 129) in 3198 dirty buckets. Tree math for 3198 random leaves in a depth-16 tree: changed internal nodes = sum_L 2^L(1-e^{-3198/2^L}) ~= 3047+2903+2648+2220+1618+978+512+256+128+64+... ~= 14.4k, so ~17.6k trie-node puts + 3284 mirror puts ~= 21k records added to the flush batch every block. Memtable evidence agrees: cf_native_trie memtable grew 116 MB plus 2 L0 flushes (<=128 MiB each) and cf_native_hashed 104 MB in 300 s ~= 0.47 GB, ~19% of the node's memtable/flush churn (591 MB memtable delta + 1.89 GB flush_write_bytes), i.e. ~19% of the 245 s compaction CPU ~= 0.15 core; plus W's root CPU (flush worker 21% CPU/node, root = 28% of its wall, plus 8 scoped hash workers) ~= 0.1-0.15 core. Total ~0.3 core/node ~= 0.9 of 18 host cores (5%) on a host running at run-queue 41-48. Write path: W's 4.1 MB batch takes 163 ms (p50 128-256 ms) with disk util avg 15%/p90 32%, so write_db is memtable-insert/lock bound and the trie's ~21k records are roughly half of its records (~50-80 ms). Removing the trie records cuts W's batch occupancy by ~50-80 ms, worth ~15-20 ms per native commit on the consensus thread (~1.5 views/commit -> ~10-13 ms of a ~650 ms view ~= 1.5-2%). CPU relief: s64 item 6's drain-window scaling (freeing ~0.35-0.4 of host CPU gave ~+17%) applied to 5% of host CPU ~= +2%. ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In /home/18c/projects/wt/s63-body-fetch/crates/torus-state/src/native_trie.rs `bucket_id` (:98) add a versioned rule: for tag 0 (CF_NATIVE_BALANCES, key = 20-byte trader, position.rs:278-294) and tag 2 (CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS, key = trader(20)||market_id(8), crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:202) take the top 16 bits of keccak(0xFF || trader) so an account's balance and its <=10 positions land in one bucket; keep keccak(cf_tag||key) for order_books/oracle/staking (level rows would otherwise make market-hot buckets). Mirror key stays bucket||tag||key so canonical (tag,key) order inside the bucket is unchanged. Bump a NATIVE_TRIE_VERSION constant checked at boot (rebuild via build_native_trie_to_cf when it differs), re-pin `charpin_*` tests and `dense_buckets` (native_trie.rs:2449-2689), keep `native_root_full` as the oracle. Accounts touched per block are bounded by dirty balances (one balance row per trader): 472/blk. ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Store per-action digests in the mempool entry at ingress: the EIP-712 trust key (`verified_cache_key_with_scratch`, torus-types/src/lib.rs:988-1002, already computed at ingress and thrown away) and `keccak(action.canonical_bytes())` (the exec sort key, native_executor.rs:6053). 2) In `dispatch_to_exec` (app.rs:5389) look the committed actions up by hash_index and attach `Vec<Option<(B256 trust_key, B256 sort_key)>>` to `CommittedBlockMsg`; pool misses stay `None`. 3) In `batch_verify_impl` (eip712.rs:1105-1112) accept a precomputed key per action and skip the sequential encode+keccak pre-pass for those; a `None` falls through to today's path (so followers with a pool miss are unchanged). 4) In `sort_native_actions` accept precomputed sort keys (fallback: compute). 5) Pass `torus_block` by value from `execution_loop` (app.rs:2307-2321 owns it) and move actions into `sender_actions` instead of `signed.action.clone()` (app.rs:1750) plus the second `action.clone()` in `sort_native_actions` (native_executor.rs:6034). Golden test: senders and order identical with and without carried keys; the sort key value is unchanged so execution order is unchanged (no consensus-visible change).
ideas.reasoning: Exec verify is 42.5 ms/native block at a 100% trust-cache hit rate (val0 histogram: 164/383 blocks <=32 ms, 323 <=64 ms). Under load it is not: the r3 note in app.rs:1606-1610 records that one small header put on the exec thread measured 60-90 ms/blk because it queued behind the background trade writer's batch. On the leader the feed runs before its header broadcast (s64 V1), so this is on the critical path. After the 0.6x late-window dilution: +0.2-1.0% matched/s. The generator holds 256 permits, so the server front is saturated: the monitor's trivial eth_blockNumber calls (same reqwest pool) succeed only 262-300 times of ~612 attempts (0.5 s cadence) in every CONC-bound cell, versus 353-555 of ~644 in RATE=270 cells. ideas.title: Mode-3 level digest: `chunked_top` is O(all chunks of the level) per save, and chunks scale with depth because chunk index is absolute per-book seq / 64

ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:2031-2085 `take_level_ops_chunked` calls `chunked_top` (:2204-2230) for every journaled level; `chunked_top` folds ALL chunks of the level and keccaks a 40 B x chunks preimage. Two steps: (S) probe: raise LEVEL_CHUNK_SEQS 64 -> 512/1024 behind a `TORUS_BOOK_ROWS` sub-mode so a deep level has ~25-50 orders per chunk (top cost /8-/16, per-dirty-chunk keccak <= ~8 KB); (M) proper fix as mode 4: two-level aggregation, super-chunk = 64 consecutive chunk idxs with a cached digest, level_hash = keccak(domain || count || qty || super-chunk (idx, digest) list); per save the cost is O(dirty chunks) + O(dirty super-chunks x 64) + O(chunks/64). Also add a gauge for total live chunks (level_chunks entries) to confirm the density estimate before building. 2) Evidence that changes existing estimates: (a) s64 item 7 (parallel cancel-all) is sized against phase1 = 111 ms; the per-minute series shows phase1 is 19 ms at 0.68M resting and 216 ms at 2.67M, so any A/B result depends on where in the cell it is measured and the item is a late-window lever only; parallelising 10 markets leaves the O(depth) term. (c) The allocator probe (s64 section 5) should be expected to change RSS, not throughput: books, memtables and queues account for ~4-4.5 GB of the 7.2 GB, the rest looks like retention.

3) Possible bugs noticed: `torus_rocksdb_block_cache_bytes` reads 87 (bytes) in metrics-after-val0.txt while the cache is 256 MiB (main.rs:1080-1092 property parse). The book_rows.rs:52-55 comment claims the mode-3 digest is depth-independent; `chunked_top` (order_book.rs:2204-2230) is O(chunks) and chunks scale with depth because chunk idx = per-book seq / 64.

ideas.title: RocksDB is compiled without SSE4.2/PCLMUL: every WAL/SST byte gets software CRC32C — add -C target-cpu=x86-64-v3 to the bench build
ideas.area: build-config / torus-state (RocksDB C++ via librocksdb-sys) + whole-workspace codegen
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) In the worktree `.cargo/config.toml` (`[target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu] rustflags`), add `"-C", "target-cpu=x86-64-v3"` next to the existing mold link-arg (or the narrower `-C target-feature=+sse4.2,+pclmulqdq,+avx2,+bmi1,+bmi2,+lzcnt`). Cargo recomputes `CARGO_CFG_TARGET_FEATURE` from RUSTFLAGS, and librocksdb-sys' build.rs (registry librocksdb-sys-0.17.3+10.4.2/build.rs:117-149) only passes `-msse4.2`/`-mpclmul`/`-mavx2`/`-mbmi` to cc when those names appear there. 2) Full rebuild into a fresh target dir (RUSTFLAGS change invalidates every crate incl. the ~10 min RocksDB C++ build; sccache keys on flags). 3) Verify with `strings`/`objdump -d` that `crc32c_3way` exists in the binary, or simply compare `torus_rocksdb_*` CPU and view timers in an interleaved n=3 A/B at cap 200. Keep this in the bench-host config only, or add a second `--config` for production builds.
ideas.reasoning: `rustc --print cfg` on the stable 1.97 toolchain gives target_feature = fxsr,sse,sse2 only, so librocksdb-sys' feature block never fires and RocksDB's util/crc32c.cc `Choose_Extend()` (line 1106-1128) falls to `ExtendImpl<DefaultCRC32>` (table-driven, ~1.5-2 GB/s) instead of `crc32c_3way` (SSE4.2+PCLMUL, ~15-20 GB/s); RocksDB has no runtime x86 detection any more (comment at crc32c.cc:1117). Volume per node per cell (ctl-r3 val0 metrics-after): wal_bytes 14.50 GB + flush_write 2.12 GB + compact_write 2.56 GB + compact_read 3.43 GB (read-side verify) ≈ 22.6 GB CRC'd in ~450 s. At 1.75 GB/s that is ~13 s CPU vs ~1.3 s with the hardware path: ~11-12 s saved per node per cell ≈ 2.5% of one core per node, ~8% of one core across the 3 co-hosted nodes. On the consensus critical path the share is small: a ≤4.1 MB body (body_push_max_bytes=4103408) costs ~2.3 ms of CRC inside the 152 ms insert_persist (~1.5%), i.e. ~0.4% of the 575 ms load-window view. The same one-liner also compiles the Rust side for x86-64-v3 (mulx/adx for the i128 FixedPoint arithmetic in the engine, AVX2 for hashbrown/memcmp/borsh loops); typical gain on integer-heavy Rust is 0-3%, applied to engine=447 ms/block on the exec thread that bounds the last ~2 min of each cell. Combined: +1-3% matched/s, mostly from lower background CPU pressure and the exec-bound tail.

ideas.title: Profile-guided optimization (PGO) of torus-node using a matched-bench cell as the training run
ideas.area: build-config (rustc -Cprofile-generate/-Cprofile-use)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Build once with `RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-generate=/tmp/pgo-data"` into its own target dir (sccache wrapper off for this build). 2) Run one short cell (e.g. 120 s, cap 200, the record env) with that binary; each node writes .profraw at exit (SIGTERM must reach normal exit — run-cell.sh already stops nodes gracefully; verify files appear). 3) Merge: `llvm-profdata merge -o merged.profdata /tmp/pgo-data/*.profraw` using the llvm-profdata that matches rustc 1.97's LLVM (install `rustup component add llvm-tools` or use `cargo-pgo`; /usr/bin/llvm-profdata-18 is likely too old for the profraw version). 4) Rebuild with `-Cprofile-use=merged.profdata -Cllvm-args=-pgo-warn-missing-function` and run the interleaved n=3 A/B. Combine with the already-listed thin-LTO/codegen-units=1 item for the full effect (PGO benefits from LTO inlining decisions).
ideas.reasoning: PGO drives inlining, block layout, and branch weights from real data; on branchy, allocation-heavy Rust (serialization, BTreeMap/VecDeque order books, hashbrown, HotStuff state machine) reported gains are typically 5-15% CPU (rustc itself ~10-20%, RocksDB/ClickHouse ~5-10%). The relevant CPU legs here: exec thread engine=447 ms/block + save_books=114 ms (exec-bound tail of every cell), and on hotstuff-algo block_build=276, insert_persist=152, on_committed_block ~120 ms of the 575 ms load-window view; hotstuff-algo on_cpu/blk=137.6 ms. If PGO cuts CPU legs by ~8%: exec-side block_ms 660→~610 (tail-window throughput +5-8%), consensus-side view shortens by ~0.08×(276+152+120 partially overlapped) ≈ 20-35 ms of 575 (3-6%). Because ~70% of the hotstuff thread's time is waiting, not computing, the whole-cell matched/s gain is diluted: estimate +2-6%.

Add `k`,`n` to `NativeDaShardRequest` (codec.rs:603-607) so the requester's params drive the layout (the fetcher already groups by (root,k,n,body_len) in shard_recovery.rs:47-52, so a mismatch just falls through to whole-body pull). 3) Keep `CF_NATIVE_SHARDS` registered (cf.rs:119, layout compatibility) but stop writing it. 4) Validate: unit test that served shard == the shard the old `put_shards_batch` would have stored (encode is deterministic, erasure.rs 'Determinism' + `encode_is_deterministic` test); then ONE 3-cell A/B with `TORUS_SHARD_CUSTODY=1` on the old code vs the new code to record the real `torus_validate_block_custody_seconds` the gate has hidden since 8fa6ccd.
ideas.reasoning: In Phase A every node already holds every body durably (ingress mirror + `mirror_native_to_da` in validate, the S459 rule), so the shards are a pure function of bytes the node has. Storing them buys nothing the serve path cannot recompute in ~0.5 ms per 21 KB body, and the recovery path fires zero times in every s65 control cell (native_da_pull_requests_total 0, shard_recovered_total 0 on all 3 nodes). What custody ON costs today, per block, per node, on the hotstuff thread: body set ~4.2 MB (direct-path pre-zstd bytes 1.28 GB over ~150 leader blocks x 2 peers); shard bytes = n/k x body = 1.5 x 4.2 = 6.3 MB; keccak passes = 1 (merkle_root in encode) + n (each `EncodedBody::proof(i)` re-runs `merkle_levels` over all shards, erasure.rs:246-248 via shard_store.rs:64) = 4 x 6.3 MB = 25 MB at the s64 248 MB/s = ~100 ms; RS parity (pure-Rust galois_8, reed-solomon-erasure 6.0.0 without simd-accel) ~4-8 ms; bincode re-serialize of 200 bodies + StoredShard clone/serialize (2 x 6.3 MB copies) ~6-10 ms; a 600-put, 6.3 MB WriteBatch + WAL, scaled from commit_persist (~4.2 MB in 39-54 ms) ~40-60 ms. Total ~150-180 ms per block on EVERY validator (validate_block) and on the leader (produce_block). Against a 620-660 ms view that is +23-27% view time, i.e. production with custody ON would run ~18-21% fewer blk/s than the bench reports. Lazy custody removes all of it: production == bench, and CF_NATIVE_SHARDS growth (6.3 MB/block, never evicted, no remove path) disappears.

ideas.title: Compute the shard Merkle tree once per body: O(1) proofs instead of n full re-hashes
ideas.area: torus-state erasure.rs / shard_store.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In `encode` (crates/torus-state/src/erasure.rs:279-311) keep the `merkle_levels` result in `EncodedBody` (e.g. `levels: Vec<Vec<B256>>`) and make `EncodedBody::proof(index)` walk the stored levels (sibling lookup per level) instead of calling `merkle_proof(&self.shards, index)`, which recomputes `merkle_levels` and keccaks every shard again. Also change `leaf_hash` (erasure.rs:154-160) to feed `Keccak256::update` with the tag, index and shard slice instead of allocating and copying a `1+4+len` buffer per shard. Keep `verify_shard` unchanged (wire format identical). Test: existing `proof_accepts_valid_rejects_corrupt` and a new assert that `proof(i)` equals the old `merkle_proof` output for every i.
ideas.reasoning: `StoredShard::from_encoded_body` (shard_store.rs:57-73) is called for i in 0..n per body, and each call re-hashes all n shards. Keccak passes per body = 1 (root) + n (proofs). At n=3: 4 passes x 6.3 MB = 25 MB -> ~100 ms/block/node -> 1 pass = 25 ms (-75 ms, about -11% of a 660 ms view if custody is ON). At the 21-validator cap (k=7, n=21): shard bytes = 3 x body = 12.6 MB, 22 passes = 277 MB keccak = ~1.1 s per block per node, i.e. custody alone would exceed the whole view; with the fix ~50 ms. Extra memcpy removed: 6.3 MB (n=3) to 12.6 MB (n=21) per block. This matters whenever shards actually have to be materialized: today's stored custody in production, the serve-on-demand path of idea 1, and any future Phase B dispersal.

ideas.title: Move the commit-boundary WAL fsync off the hotstuff thread before production turns it on
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs persist path / torus-state db.rs sync_wal
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: `TORUS_SYNC_WAL_ON_COMMIT` (crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:916-934, default OFF, never A/B'd: docs/plans/commit-fsync-durability-impl.md Task 4 has no result) runs `state_db.sync_wal()` inline inside the commit persist path (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:941-960), i.e. inside `on_committed_block` on the hotstuff thread (already ~120 ms in the load window). Change it to: after the header/body/manifest batch is written, hand a `sync_wal` request to the existing flush worker (or a dedicated 'torus-wal-sync' thread) with a per-commit sequence number; record `torus_commit_wal_sync_seconds` and a lag gauge (commits whose fsync is still pending). Anything that must observe crash-durability (RPC finality reporting, the S459 'durable before referenced' invariant when it is later tightened to fsync) waits on the sequence number, not the consensus thread. Then run ONE custody-off cell with the flag ON, inline vs off-thread, to put the real fsync cost on record.
ideas.reasoning: The shared RocksDB WAL on val0 grew 12.57 GB in the 300 s load window (torus_rocksdb_wal_bytes delta, s65-votefix-ctl-r2), 42 MB/s, ~31 MB per committed block (403 commits) because CF_NATIVE_PENDING ingress mirrors, commit bodies, exec state and trade history all share one WAL (s64 item 9 note). A `flush_wal(true)` per commit must drain whatever of that is still dirty to a QEMU virtual disk (lsblk: sda QEMU HARDDISK); on such disks a flush is typically 5-50 ms and is latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Inline, that lands directly on the critical path already identified as the bottleneck (the leader runs the commit feed before broadcasting, s64 V1; planned item C moves it after the proposal but still on the same thread). Off-thread, the same durability is reached one fsync later (bounded, measurable lag) with zero consensus-thread cost. Estimate: if fsync is 15-45 ms per commit at ~1.5 commits per view, inline costs 22-68 ms of a 620-660 ms view = -3-10% blk/s in production; off-thread ~0%.

ideas.title: Carry per-action digests into exec: stop hashing the ~4 MB body twice and cloning it twice on the exec thread per block
ideas.area: torus-consensus app.rs execute_committed_block + torus-types eip712.rs batch_verify_impl + torus-bridge sort_native_actions
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Two variants. (S, no format change) In eip712.rs batch_verify_impl (~L1100-1112) compute the trust-cache keys in an order-preserving rayon map instead of the sequential `actions.iter().map(verified_cache_key_with_scratch)` pre-pass, keeping only the FifoCache lookups sequential; in native_executor.rs sort_native_actions/sort_deterministic (L6026-6070) hash the sort keys in parallel and sort a Vec of indices/references instead of cloning every (Address, NativeAction) pair, and change app.rs:1750 `signed.action.clone()` to borrow (execute_batch already borrows via FlatAction). (M, full) Store `verified_key` (planned by s64 #4) plus `keccak(canonical_bytes)` in the NativePoolEntry at ingress (the canonical buffer is already built there); have `remove_committed_native` at app.rs:5446-5455 return the entries' digests and attach a `Vec<Option<(B256,B256)>>` to `CommittedBlockMsg` (app.rs:5460); exec uses them for the trust-cache pre-pass and the sort key, computing only for `None` (bodies reconstructed from DA).
ideas.reasoning: Canonical bytes per order are 45-53 B (torus-types encode_place_order_params), so a 400-order batch is ~18-21 KB and a 197-action block is 3.6-4.2 MB. At the ~250 MB/s keccak rate the s64 report measured, one full pass is 15-17 ms. The exec thread does that pass twice per block: once in the sequential trust-cache pre-pass (still run when every action hits; misses were 0) and once for `action_sort_key`. Add the two 5 MB deep clones (app.rs:1750 and the sort pair) and the two encode passes: ~35-40 ms of a 715 ms exec chain, i.e. ~5%. The measured numbers agree: exec_verify is 45.9 ms with 0 misses (nothing else in that phase is expensive when every action hits), and the untimed E-side residual (chain 715.4 minus verify 45.9 + replay 8.1 + engine 481.9 + save_books 131.4 + state_write_build 25.2 + handoff 1.1 + body_persist 0.6 + load_books 0.1) is ~21 ms, which is exactly what the sort's clone+keccak should cost. The late ~120 s of each cell is exec-bound (busy 0.91-0.93), so ~5% less exec work there is ~5% more fills there; the early window is consensus-bound, so ~0 there. On the 300 s average that is roughly 0.4 x 5% = +2%, range +1.5-3%, and it raises the exec ceiling that s64 #1 (deferred commit feed) will otherwise hit. The S variant on an 8-thread rayon pool keeps ~5-8 ms of the 35-40 ms.

ideas.title: Bounded nonce replay guard: exec-time nonce-window rule, in-RAM recent-nonce set, pruned CF_NATIVE_NONCES (MultiGet as the no-consensus-change fallback)

ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Add a deterministic exec-time validity rule mirroring ingress: an action whose nonce is outside header.timestamp +/- NONCE_WINDOW_MS is dropped (FIX-2 style drop-and-log, never slash) in the app.rs:1708-1750 loop and in validator.rs:355-390. 2) With that rule, a (sender, nonce) can only be replayed within ~2 x 60 s of block timestamps, so replace the 200 per-action `StateBackend::get_cf_raw(overlay, CF_NATIVE_NONCES, ..)` reads with an exec-thread HashSet<(Address,u64)> of nonces consumed in the last 2 x window (~214/s x 120 s ~ 26k entries), pruned by nonce; seed it at boot from the CF (or the last ~120 s of committed bodies). 3) Bound the CF: re-key as nonce(8 BE) || sender(20) so a periodic `delete_range_cf` up to (ts - 2 x window) prunes it, or attach a compaction filter on the height value. Keep the 200 puts (or drop them once the RAM set is the authority and the boot seed comes from bodies). Interim S variant with no consensus change: replace the 200 gets with one `multi_get_cf` on the 200 keys after checking own-pending/parent overlays.

ideas.title: Ingress: stop the per-submit JSON re-encode + keccak for the ack hash and the duplicate canonical/bincode encodes (one encode per submitted action)
ideas.area: torus-rpc torus.rs submit path + torus-mempool lib.rs/native_pool.rs insert + torus-state native_da.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: In torus-rpc torus.rs verify_one_action_with (L273-306): return keccak256 of the raw decoded input `bytes` (already in hand) or the pool's action hash instead of `serde_json::to_writer(action)` + keccak; keep the JSON hash only for the JSON endpoint if the API contract must hold. In torus-mempool: compute the canonical buffer once per submit and derive both `compute_action_hash` and `verified_cache_key` from it (the preimages differ by a single 0x00 tag byte, torus-types lib.rs), passing the hash into `insert_verified` (native_pool.rs:151-160 currently recomputes it) and into `NativeDaStore::put_batch` (native_da.rs:87-100 recomputes it again and bincode-serializes again). For `--format bin` ingress keep the client's bincode bytes and reuse them as the DA value and the gossip payload body instead of re-serializing; drop one of the two action clones on lib.rs:380-383 / 766 by moving the action into the DA pending buffer by reference-counted Arc.
ideas.reasoning: Per accepted submit the ingress node currently does: hex parse, bincode decode, EIP-712 struct hash (400 small keccaks) + ecrecover, serde_json of the whole 400-order batch + keccak (ack only), canonical encode + keccak (cache key), canonical encode + keccak (pool action hash), bincode serialized_size walk, DA bincode encode + another canonical encode + keccak, gossip bincode encode, and 2-3 full clones. The JSON pass alone is 60-100 KB (0.2-0.4 ms to serialize, 0.25-0.4 ms to keccak); the redundant canonical+keccak passes ~0.15 ms; DA/gossip re-encodes ~0.1 ms: ~0.75-1.05 ms CPU per submit. At 107,294 accepted submits per node per 300 s (358/s) that is 0.27-0.38 core per node, ~0.8-1.1 cores across the three co-hosted validators on an 18-core host whose run queue is 41-48 under load. ideas.title: Fees: native trading fees are never accrued today; when they land, account them per trader per block (not per fill) so they do not regress the exec ceiling
ideas.area: torus-bridge native_executor.rs settlement + distribute_fees; torus-core position.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Nothing to remove today: `total_native_fees` is declared (native_executor.rs:1457), zeroed (L1880) and read (L5805) but never incremented, so `distribute_fees` early-returns every block and no per-fill fee work exists. When fee charging is implemented, do it as: (a) per-market settle workers accumulate (trader -> fee) and (market -> fee) in worker-local maps during Phase 4 (same pattern as maker_margin_releases), (b) merge in market-id order and apply one BalanceCache read-modify-write per trader per block, (c) credit the treasury row once per block and add the block total to `total_native_fees`, (d) never touch the overlay per fill. Add a differential test that per-fill and per-block accounting produce byte-identical balances.
ideas.reasoning: This is a design guard rather than a gain today. With 58,118 fills per native block, a naive per-fill implementation would add two balance RMWs (taker and maker) per fill plus a treasury credit: even through the in-memory BalanceCache that is ~116k map hits (~15-25 ms/block, 2-3% of the 715 ms exec chain); through overlay puts per fill (Borsh encode + RwLock + journal) it would be ~1-2 us per put x 116k = 120-230 ms/block, a 16-32% exec regression. The per-trader-per-block form costs one RMW per active trader (5,000 senders) per block, under 1 ms. Expected improvement now is 0%; the value is avoiding a -3..-30% exec regression when fees are switched on, which matters because the late window is already exec-bound.

ideas.risk: Per-block fee application changes the intra-block point at which a trader's balance drops, which can interact with the defensive `.min(order_margin)` clamps and margin checks for later orders in the same block; the differential test must cover a trader whose fee exhausts `available` mid-block.

1) Possible bug / product gap: native trading fees are never charged. `total_native_fees` has no increment site anywhere in crates/, so `distribute_fees` (native_executor.rs:5800-5823) is a no-op every block and there is no fee revenue for the reward distributor. Not a throughput issue, but it means the "fees" part of this angle has zero per-action cost today, and every bench number excludes whatever fee accounting will cost later.
2) Evidence that refines s64 item 4/§5 ('exec verify 44 ms despite 0 misses -> skip the rayon phase'): with 0 misses the rayon phase does nothing; the 46 ms is dominated by the sequential trust-cache key pre-pass in eip712.rs batch_verify_impl (canonical encode + keccak of ~4 MB, 15-20 ms at 250 MB/s) plus whatever is left unattributed. Skipping the rayon phase would save little; removing or parallelising the pre-pass is the lever (idea 1). A timer split inside batch_verify_impl (pre-pass vs Phase 1 vs Phase 2) would settle the remaining ~25 ms.
3) Untimed exec residual: exec_chain 715.4 ms minus all E-side timers (verify 45.9, replay 8.1, engine 481.9, save_books 131.4, state_write_build 25.2, handoff 1.1, body_persist 0.6, load_books 0.1) leaves ~21 ms per native block that no timer covers; sort_native_actions (clone + keccak of canonical bytes, native_executor.rs:6026-6070) sits exactly in that gap. The FIFO cache (cap 32,000 via TORUS_VERIFIED_SENDER_CACHE_CAP) recorded 75,294 evictions per node per cell, i.e. it churns ~2.3x; misses are still 0 today, but a longer nonce backlog or a bigger pool could start missing and each miss costs a full ecrecover on the exec thread.

ideas.title: Deduplicate body fetches: one third of served bodies and 36% of received bodies are duplicates in a healthy cell
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs networking/receiving.rs filter_message, hotstuff/implementation.rs on_receive_proposal_header / request_missing_parent / tick_missing_pc_block_fetch / on_receive_block_data_request
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: (1) Header double-processing: receiving.rs filter_message inserts a future-view ProposalHeader into msg_buffer AND returns it immediately because is_block_data_msg() (hotstuff/messages.rs:106-113) includes ProposalHeader; when the view advances the buffered copy is replayed and on_receive_proposal_header (implementation.rs ~2073-2100) sends a second BlockDataRequest and overwrites body_fetch_tracker with no in-flight check. Fix: in on_receive_proposal_header skip the request (and the tracker reset) when body_fetch_tracker already holds block_hash, keeping the replay for the vote; or make filter_message return-once for headers (do not also buffer what it already delivered). (2) Parallel retry trains: enter_view's deferred-proposal branch and tick_missing_pc_block_fetch (implementation.rs:2920-2975) call request_missing_parent -> request_justify_block, which dedups only against justify_fetch_tracker (~2766), not pending_headers/body_fetch_tracker, so a second 100 ms x 9 train (tick_justify_fetch_retries) runs beside the header-path train for the same body. Fix: skip when pending_headers/body_fetch_tracker has the hash and its first request is younger than BODY_FETCH_DEADLINE, or merge the two trackers. (3) Cheap belt-and-braces: in on_receive_block_data_request (2119-2151) remember (hash, peer, Instant) of the last serve and skip a repeat within ~50 ms. (4) Optional: make BODY_RETRY_INTERVAL (2988, 100 ms) adaptive, e.g. max(100 ms, 2x EWMA of observed header->body). Validate with TORUS_BODY_FETCH_TRACE=1: requests per (hash,peer) should drop to ~1.0 and untracked receives to ~0; add a unit test that a header delivered out-of-view then replayed produces exactly one BlockDataRequest.
ideas.reasoning: val0 in s65-votefix-fix-r1 load window (02:49:26-02:54:31 UTC, body_fetch_diag stamps): 526 BlockDataRequests served for 353 distinct (hash,peer) pairs = 173 duplicates (33%); 108 of the 173 arrive <50 ms after the first (p10 0.19 ms, p50 29 ms) which is far below the 100 ms retry and matches the header replay; 35 land in 50-150 ms (the 100 ms retry firing while the first 4 MB response is still in flight; header->body p90 is 120-134 ms per the s64 report); 30 are >150 ms. On the receive side 538 responses for 343 hashes: 195 (36%) arrive untracked (tracked_header=false, retries=None) and are discarded by park_pushed_body (body > 64 KiB cap) after sitting in the inbound queue a mean of 285 ms; per-hash response counts reach 5-6 (10 hashes) and 14 (1 hash). 77 receives are tracked_justify=true, 71 of them with local_view = response_view+1, i.e. the by-hash missing-parent train firing for a body already in flight. Bytes: (173+195) x 4.1 MB ~ 1.5 GB per node per 300 s = 5 MB/s per node, ~15 MB/s host-wide of borsh encode/decode plus QUIC AES-GCM, on tokio workers that total ~38% of a core for val0 (threads.log: 18 tokio-rt-worker x 2.1%). Arithmetic: 15 MB/s x (encode+decode+crypto ~ 2-3 ms/MB/side) ~ 3-5% of one core host-wide = <=0.3% of 18 cores, so the CPU gain is small. Latency: ~100 of the 173 duplicates are requested inside the ~25-30 ms transfer window of the first copy and share the proposer's outbound QUIC connection, delaying the needed copy by an estimated 5-10 ms on ~30% of bodies = 2-3 ms per ~620 ms view (0.4%), plus fewer 4 MB decodes blocking the swarm task ahead of votes/headers. Net: +0-2% matched/s; the certain wins are ~35% less body traffic, less queue/memory churn and a shorter p99 body tail (462-608 ms today).

ideas.title: Give write-once, short-lived CFs their own RocksDB options: FIFO+TTL compaction for CF_NATIVE_PENDING (and shards), drop bottommost Zstd for churny CFs
ideas.area: torus-state db.rs (StateDb::open per-CF options), native_da.rs
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:278-291 builds ONE cf_opts for all 44 CFs (128 MiB memtable, LZ4, bottommost Zstd, level_compaction_dynamic_level_bytes); only CF_CONSENSUS_META and the three churny CFs override the write-buffer size (:293-323). Add per-CF option sets: (1) CF_NATIVE_PENDING and CF_NATIVE_SHARDS -> set_compaction_style(Fifo) with FifoCompactionOptions (TTL ~1 h, max_table_files_size bound) and plain LZ4 (no bottommost Zstd): bodies are content-hash keyed (native_da.rs:87-107, uniformly random 32-byte keys), never deleted (s64 §4 bug 8) and only needed until the referencing block is committed — persist_committed_block_durably (app.rs:853-900) copies the full body into CF_BLOCK_BODIES at commit, and the 60 s nonce window bounds selection. (2) For CF_BOOK_ORDER_ROWS / CF_NATIVE_ORDER_BOOKS / CF_NATIVE_HASHED (rewritten every block) use LZ4 at the bottommost level too, trading disk space for compaction CPU. Keep the RocksDB LOG from the A/B cell so per-CF compaction bytes can be checked.
ideas.reasoning: rocksdb:low (compaction) is the largest single CPU consumer on every node in the load window: 68.5% / 78.3% / 81.5% (threads.log), and torus_rocksdb_compaction_cpu_micros is 251-263 CPU-seconds per node per cell. The DA store ingests every submitted body: 93,867 x ~28 KB ~= 2.6 GB raw per node per cell (~23% of the 11.6 GB WAL) as random-keyed, never-deleted data; under leveled compaction with dynamic level sizing each byte is rewritten several times and re-compressed with Zstd at the bottom level where ~90% of the data lives. FIFO compaction never rewrites: files are only dropped by age/size, so this stream's compaction cost goes to ~0. Estimate: the DA CF plausibly accounts for 30-50% of compaction CPU (random keys, largest never-deleted stream) -> 75-125 CPU-s per cell per node ~= 0.25-0.4 core per node ~= 0.75-1.2 cores host-wide; LZ4 bottommost on the churny CFs removes the Zstd share of the remainder. At ~1-3% throughput per core freed (s64 item-6 sensitivity) that is +1-3%, plus it fixes the unbounded DA growth (bug 8) and the 48%-util disk write load.

ideas.title: Exec verify: pass the trust-cache keys with the block so the exec thread's pre-pass is a lookup, not 200 canonical encodes + keccaks
ideas.area: torus-types eip712.rs batch_verify_impl, torus-consensus app.rs dispatch_to_exec / execute_committed_block_with, torus-mempool native_pool
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: batch_verify_impl (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1105-1112) runs a SEQUENTIAL pre-pass that calls verified_cache_key_with_scratch for every action; that function (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:988-1002) canonically encodes the whole 400-order batch (~24 KB) and keccaks it. Planned item (A)/(C)'s companion, s64 item 4, stores this key in the pool entry so the commit-side restash becomes a lookup — extend it one step: dispatch_to_exec (app.rs:5389) puts the keys (Vec<Option<B256>>, taken from the pool entries via the same hash_index lookup verified_restash_keys uses, native_pool.rs:114-131) next to native_actions in the exec message, and batch_verify_native_actions_cached takes an optional precomputed-key slice (compute only where None). par_recover then returns the cached sender for every hit as it already does (eip712.rs:969-977).
ideas.reasoning: torus_exec_verify_seconds is 44.95 ms per native block (n=345) while the trust cache reports 120,780 hits and 0 misses, so no ecrecover runs; the cost is the pre-pass. Arithmetic: a 400-order PlaceOrderBatch canonical encoding is ~24 KB -> ~180 keccak-f blocks at ~0.5 us plus ~40 us of encoding ~= 130 us per action x 200 actions ~= 26 ms, plus 200 RwLock lookups and the rayon dispatch. The exec thread spends ~710 ms per native block (verify 45 + replay guard 8 + engine 509 + save_books drain 146, whole-cell means), and the last ~120 s of every 300 s cell are exec-bound (exec busy 0.91-0.93). Removing ~30 ms is -4% of exec-thread time -> +4% blk/s in the exec-bound window -> about +1.5-2.5% on the 300 s average, and it raises the exec ceiling that the planned commit-feed deferral (C) will run into.

ideas.title: Stop re-verifying every gossiped action on every validator: origin-attested gossip plus a pre-exec verify stage for committed blocks only
ideas.area: torus-node main.rs gossip ingest, torus-mempool add_native_action_from_gossip, torus-network native-action topic, torus-consensus execution_loop
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: Each non-RPC validator runs a gossip-verify pool at half the cores (crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:648-687) and add_native_action_from_gossip (crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:482-527) does: DA mirror (clone + bincode + RocksDB), verified_cache_key (canonical encode + keccak), recover_sender (EIP-712 struct hash: 400 item keccaks + 400 recomputed typehash keccaks, eip712.rs:285-316, then ecrecover), then admit -> compute_action_hash again. Change: the origin validator signs (sender, action_hash) with its validator key and gossips (sender, action, origin_sig); receivers verify one ed25519 signature (~50 us), DA-mirror, and admit with verified_locally=false. Add a pre-exec stage: a thread that walks the exec queue ahead of execution_loop (app.rs:2307) and runs batch_verify_native_actions_cached on queued committed blocks, seeding the trust cache so the exec thread's pass hits. The RPC node keeps full ingress verification. A wrong sender under a validator signature is slashable evidence.
ideas.reasoning: Every submitted action is fully verified three times across the cluster although only 68% ever execute (native_actions_processed 64,266 of 93,867 received; s64 V6: ~37% expire unused). threads.log shows torus-gossip-verify at 105.7% / 103.7% CPU on the two non-RPC nodes and torus-ingress-verify at 106.2% on the RPC node in the load window, i.e. ~3 ms CPU per action per node against ~0.5 ms of actual crypto. With attestation the gossip nodes drop to ~0.15 core (decode, DA mirror, one ed25519 verify) and the verification moves to ~230 executed actions/s x ~1 ms (struct hash 0.7 + ecrecover 0.15 + key) ~= 0.23 core per node on a pre-exec stage that is off the exec thread (the exec queue already lags 1-3 s, so there is time). Net ~0.6 core per gossip node ~= 1.2 cores host-wide, and the last third of verified-then-expired work disappears. At ~1-3% per core freed: +1-3%.

ideas.title: Pacemaker: per-entry view deadlines instead of the stale absolute epoch schedule (rebase when BEHIND, not only when ahead)
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs pacemaker (crates/hotstuff_rs/src/pacemaker/implementation.rs update_view / update_timeouts)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) In `update_view` (pacemaker/implementation.rs:597-643) the deadline of a QC-driven entry is the ABSOLUTE slot `epoch_start_time + k*max_view_time` computed at epoch entry (`update_timeouts`, :868-902; slots are 500 ms, genesis `timeout_base_ms`=500, devnet/wsl/genesis-3val.json:8). Step 2b (:610-613) rebases the schedule only when the replica is AHEAD (`scheduled > now + 2*max_view_time*multiplier`); nothing rebases when it is BEHIND, so once loaded views run ~600-800 ms the schedule falls behind within ~4 views and every multiplier-1 entry gets a deadline already in the past → instant timeout → the next block is proposed with a non-consecutive justify → 2-chain commit does not fire → commit lag grows → the S470 commit-lag term (`commit_lag_exponent`, :1229) stretches deadlines to 1-2 s (node-locally, anchored at each node's own `Instant::now()` in 2c :629) → when commits catch up the multiplier drops to 1 and the stale schedule bites again. Add the symmetric rule: on every entry set `deadline = max(scheduled, now + max_view_time * multiplier)` (or simply rebase the schedule from `now` when `scheduled < now + max_view_time`), so a healthy QC-driven entry always gets a full slot from entry time. Keep the multiplier logic. 2) Unit tests: a replica entering view v with `scheduled < now` must get `now + max_view_time`; lockstep test that two replicas entering the same view within δ get deadlines within δ. 3) Zero-code companion A/B on the same day: genesis `timeout_base_ms` 500 → 1000 at cap 200 (the s55 500→1500 test was cap 100 / exec-bound; never re-run in the consensus-bound regime). 4) Run the `--crash-at 60` gate afterwards (liveness-only change, no safety impact).
ideas.reasoning: Measured in s65-votefix-ctl-r2 (val0 log, load window 306 s): 586 views, 403 heights, 144 view timeouts (25% of views; 20-29% in every other s65/s64 control cell, views/height 1.44-1.51 in all of them; the lighter r270 cells drop to 13-14% and 1.20 because views get shorter than the 500 ms slot). Of the 144 timeouts, 113 are instant skips (view entered and left without processing a single message); 88 of them are skipped by val1 too (fleet-wide), 25 only by val0 (desync). Skips concentrate later in each 100-view epoch (13/17/27/30/26 per 20-view bin) and the mean view duration climbs from ~525 ms at epoch positions 0-29 to ~690 ms at 40-69 — exactly what a schedule that is re-anchored only at epoch change predicts. The other ~31-42 timeouts are mid-flight: 42 views > 1.4 s total 74 s = 24% of the window; view-before-a-skip mean 1094 ms (backed-off deadline), view-after-a-skip 540 ms. Cross-node entry skew for the same view: median 23 ms but p90 501 ms, max 1935 ms; with a 3/3 quorum (`quorum()` = 2/3*power+1, validator_set.rs:153) the fleet waits for the slowest node's stretched deadline (example: view 730 — val0 sat in it 1.85 s while val1 had timed out 730 and 731 and proposed 732 at +1.66 s). Arithmetic: ~55-74 s of 306 s are timed-out wall time (18-24%); removing it gives +15-24% consensus-side blk/s; with the s64 dilution (0.6x, late window exec-bound) and the ~+25% early-window exec cap → +6-12% matched/s, plus commit-interval p95 (3.4 s) shrinks because consecutive justifies return (views/height 1.47 → ~1.1, cf. s55 1.50 → 1.07).

ideas.title: Body-fetch retry timer (100 ms) fires below the loaded p90 header→body RTT, producing ~40% duplicate body requests and responses
ideas.area: hotstuff_rs body fetch (crates/hotstuff_rs/src/hotstuff/implementation.rs tick_pending_body_retries_at, BODY_RETRY_INTERVAL)
ideas.what_needs_to_be_done: 1) Make the first retry interval load-aware: keep an EWMA of observed header→response latency per node (the `body_fetch_tracker` already stores `first_req`) and retry at max(100 ms, 2×EWMA) — or a flat 250 ms — before rotating to other validators. 2) On the first response for a hash, drop the tracker entry immediately (it is, via try_insert_body) and ignore later copies before deserialisation on the network thread when the hash is already in the tree (swarm admission already logs the hash; add a `contains` gate). 3) Count duplicates in a metric (`body_fetch_duplicate_responses_total`).
ideas.reasoning: In s65-votefix-ctl-r2 (val0, load window) the header→first-body-response latency is p50 62 ms, p90 227 ms, p99 536 ms, max 896 ms — the RTT is dominated by the serving leader's busy HotStuff thread (commit feeds), not the network. With `BODY_RETRY_INTERVAL` = 100 ms and rotation to non-proposers at 200 ms, val0 as leader served 2.82 requests per own proposal instead of 2 (+41%), and as follower received 481 responses for 331 fetched views: 37% of views got 2-7 copies. All served on the leader's HotStuff thread (`on_receive_block_data_request`: pending_bodies clone + send) and processed on the follower's (`on_receive_block_data_response` → park_pushed_body). Because proposals are compact (datum ≈ 7 KB of hashes), each extra copy costs only ~0.1-1 ms of consensus-thread time and a few KB on the wire, so the gain is small (~0.3-0.8 ms × 1.5 per view of a ~650 ms view ≈ +0-1%). It is a real 'timer below the RTT' bug that will matter more if bodies ever travel inline (TorusBlock, up to 4 MB) or with body push on.
evidence: implementation.rs:2985-3000 BODY_RETRY_INTERVAL 100 ms, MAX_BODY_RETRIES 2, rotation; :2566-2645 retry loop; :2120-2150 serve on the algo thread

val0.log.gz body_fetch_diag parse (load window): requests per own proposal mean 2.82 (dist 2:34, 3:32, 4:8, 6-8:3); responses per fetched view 1:210, 2:90, 3:25, 4:4, 7:2; header→first response p50/p90/p99 = 62/227/536 ms; serve found=false = 0 (rotated requests always find the body)
s64 §2.8: header→body avg 45-52 ms, p99 462-608 ms (consistent)
ideas.expected_improvement: +0-1% (compact proposals); cheap insurance for full-body modes
ideas.risk: A longer first retry delays recovery from a genuinely lost first request by up to ~150 ms; bounded by the 4 s BODY_FETCH_DEADLINE.
ideas.why_new: s64 discusses body push and serving fetches off-thread but not the retry cadence; the duplicate-request/response rate under load has not been measured before.

raw.notes: 1) Reinterpretation of the s65 blocked-time result: the HotStuff thread's idle time is mostly `ProgressMessageStub::recv` → `receiver.recv_timeout` (networking/receiving.rs:177-189, called from algorithm.rs:283-301 with the view deadline), i.e. a futex wait for the NEXT message from a peer — not a user-space lock. With three ~30%-busy consensus threads chained along the critical path (leader build+feed → header → follower vote → next leader body fetch/validate/insert → QC), 70% off-CPU on any one thread is expected; it does not point at storage or at a lock. 2) Absolute schedule verification: a naive replay of the epoch slots against val0's view entries shows the schedule behind on 260 of 506 entries mid-epoch (lag up to 8.5 s by view 800), yet only 10 of those entries exit instantly — because the S470 commit-lag multiplier (bench env cap 8) is active most of the time and gives fresh 1-2 s deadlines; the instant skips cluster exactly where the multiplier returns to 1. This is why the cheapest experiment (base 1000 ms) and the code fix (rebase when behind) should be run as separate arms. 3) In view 730 (val0 leader) the header left val0 ~650 ms after entry: produce (+40 ms), selection (+125 ms), then three synchronous commit feeds (+264/+376/+495 ms) — direct confirmation of s64 item 1 (leader commit feed before header) with the 3-commit case; followers also spend ~300-450 ms per body in validate + 3 feeds (val1 34.55→34.93, val2 34.53→35.00), delaying their next header processing — supports the 'feed off-thread on all nodes' follow-up. 4) Exec-side: bucket member cache hit rate 97.8% (mc_hit 1.26 M / mc_miss 28 k) — not a cache-never-hits case; flush worker W runs 398 ms/block + state_write 196 + root 107 (~0.7 s/block on W) while E is ~0.8 busy, so W is the next exec ceiling after E. 5) Exec dispatch is the blocking `exec_tx.send` on a sync_channel(64) (app.rs:340, rate_limit.rs:299); observed exec_queue_depth max 10 → it never blocks; not a contributor. 6) `validate_block` and `on_committed_block` try `bincode::deserialize::<TorusBlock>` before the CompactBlock path (app.rs:4830-4840, log 'CompactBlock fallback' 355×) — the datum is ~7 KB so the failed attempt is negligible; not worth a change. 7) `on_commit_block` handler in torus-node (main.rs:872-890) logs the EXECUTED height for each committed block (three 'height=644' lines for commits 645-647) — same root as s64 bug 6; it runs on the event thread, so no consensus cost.
